bluf: Valtech is a Luxembourg registered experience innovation company of 6,000 people across 24 countries by its own llms.txt, founded in 1993, selling enterprise platforms, commerce and now governed AI agents to enterprise buyers. The record shows a systems integrator repositioning around AI in public: Valtech One accelerators on the homepage, an Agent Factory launched at DMEXCO 2026, a GEO QuickStart built on Adobe Brand Visibility, and four bolt-on acquisitions (Revonic, Evident, The Berndt Group, Appsolutely) folded in. The one thing a rival should know: it practises the one line the Radar could test, publishes an llms.txt, and lists delivery offices in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico and India, while 19 of its 20 named clients carry no described work.
doing:
Valtech calls itself the experience innovation company, aligning strategy, design, engineering, commerce, data and AI to modernize enterprises and turn AI potential into performance; its headline claim is $75 million+ unlocked for Discover through a financial services transformation. In plain words: a platform implementer and commerce builder that now sells AI adoption as the wrapper. The sold mix leads with Web & Product and AI Automation / Agents, both scored 3. The web and platform line is the company's identity: DXP and commerce platform offers, the Axpo Group Adobe Experience Manager migration, Optimizely DXP Partner of the Year. The AI line is Valtech One (AI accelerators) and the Intelligent Enterprise pitch on the homepage, the Agent Factory launched at DMEXCO 2026 to build and govern enterprise agents, an AI concierge commerce experience (Valtech Concierge) and a Content OS. Two lines score 2: AI Search / GEO (a GEO QuickStart page offering a 30 day AI visibility programme on Adobe Brand Visibility, and GEO blogs by its global SEO lead) and Data & Measurement (a Data & AI Revolution offering with data science, analytics and insights, and Microsoft Fabric Featured Partner status). SEO, paid search, paid social, CRO, creators and CRM each score 1; breadth is 10 of 15.

The service list runs Experience Elevation, Commerce Acceleration, Enterprise Transformation, Marketing Creativity & Performance, Data & AI Revolution, DXP, B2C and D2C commerce platforms, B2B commerce and customer portals, CRM and loyalty, product and service design, data science consulting, and optimization and personalization. Partners on record are Adobe, Optimizely, Microsoft Fabric, Salesforce (Data 360 offers appear in its LinkedIn ads) and the MACH Alliance, where it holds an award. The site markup also lists a Eurobest 2025 Silver in Social & Influencer and a 2025 Gartner Visionary placement that its own Google ads cite.

The AI posture is adoption through Valtech One accelerators, a governed Agent Factory, AI concierge commerce and the GEO QuickStart with Adobe. No pricing signal is in the record. The dated moves: the Agent Factory launch in 2026-09; undated newsroom items for the Fast Company Best Workplaces for Innovators listing, the Microsoft Fabric partner recognition, ABB Robotics choosing Valtech (scope not captured), a Mitchells & Butlers partnership announced with Hitachi Digital Services, and site banners saying Revonic, Evident, The Berndt Group and Appsolutely are now part of Valtech. Case studies dated 2026-09-23 cover Axpo, Lexus Europe and agentic AI, a leading beauty brand saving USD 20M with AI, a global flavors and fragrances leader, a French luxury maison, National Veterinary Associates and Valet. Conspicuously absent for a company of its kind: any media buying depth, any own case study with a described marketing outcome, and a detected CMS or test tool on its own site.
clients:
The book is enterprise across eleven verticals: agriculture, CPG, financial services, health, luxury, manufacturing, mobility, new space, public sector, retail, and travel and hospitality. The record lists sixteen office countries from Denmark and France to Canada, the USA, Argentina, Brazil, Mexico, China, India and Singapore, so the home market is global with a European centre. Twenty clients are named; one carries engagement evidence the classifier could read and 19 are names only.

What the evidence says: Axpo Group came for an Adobe Experience Manager migration (web build and platform, observed). Lexus Europe appears in a case study titled around agentic AI at its service, and Discover in the $75 million+ transformation headline, though the classifier reads only their names. Mandarin Oriental, Eton Shirts, Mars, Volvo Trucks, Fountain Tire, Fox, Lundbeck, PFA Pension, Sika, Dunelm, Audi, Dolby, dunnhumby, Decathlon and National Veterinary Associates are case study names and slugs with no described work; ABB Robotics and Mitchells & Butlers come from press releases with scope not captured. Because the described need is a single platform migration, the needs of this book are inferred from what Valtech leads with: platform builds, commerce, and now agents.

Six clients also sit on other tracked agencies' books: Mars with assembly and bounteous, Decathlon with epsilon and junto, Mandarin Oriental with assembly, Volvo Trucks with merkle, ABB Robotics with klientboost and Mitchells & Butlers with tug. The pattern is the same as the other integrators in the top ten: enterprises that buy their platform from Valtech buy media, search and creative elsewhere. What the base needs next, as a judgment: under KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) these clients will very likely keep buying agent, data and commerce plumbing, Valtech's own ground; under KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) the same clients are beginning to buy AI visibility, where Valtech sells a QuickStart without an audited product, which is the contestable purchase, with moderate confidence.
house: One line was testable and it passed: Valtech sells AI search and publishes an llms.txt (the file itself describes 6,000 people across 24 countries), with 10 AI topic URLs in its sitemap; the integrity score is 100 on that single test, and the Radar flags no gaps. The sitemap lists 5990 URLs with 264 updated in 90 days and 1540 in 365. It runs its own Google ads, 104 in the Transparency Center with 37 in the last 30 days (50 text, 54 image, last shown 2026-09-27) under VALTECH MEXICO, VALTECH SA and VALTECH GLOBAL PROJECTS, one reading "Valtech - Gartner Visionary 2025 | Trusted by L'Oréal, Mars and Volkswagen". It runs 22+ LinkedIn ads (21 company page, 1 thought leader), several in Spanish selling Salesforce Data 360. GTM is the only tag detected; no CMS, pixel or test tool was identified, and no AI crawlers are blocked. Its own channels link LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube and Facebook.
market:
The Horus read is Favored at +30.3, the 89th percentile, with the sold mix at 15:32 on the Solar Arc (afternoon) and no headwind judgment at all. It is best placed for KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer) through Data & Measurement and AI Automation / Agents, and for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) through AI Search / GEO. Best scenario fit is The Bazaar of Agents at 53; resilience 39.1. Of the eight moves it is partial on an audited AI visibility product (P1), on retraining juniors into agent operators (P6) and on owned audiences (P7); absent on feeds and entities (P2) and on testing ads inside assistants (P8); LSAs and paid inputs (P3, P4) do not apply; pricing on outcomes (P5) is unknown to the record.

The Monsoon read is Onshore wind at 61.0, the 71st percentile: 55 of it is the sold mix, with web build and agent engineering carrying the most movable hours. Migration 72.0 against displacement 50.0, and the migration side is observed: offices listed in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico and India plus 6,000 people, offset by an enterprise client base. The shore split, tilted toward that footprint, points 50% to South and Southeast Asia and 31% to Eastern Europe. No onshore delivery claim appears in the record.
openings:
Valtech is very unlikely to be beaten on platform engineering by a marketing agency; the openings sit around the platform. First, the observed delivery footprint in Argentina, Brazil, Mexico and India with migration at 72: an onshore, senior led delivery pitch has something concrete to point at, and it is likely to land with the European enterprise clients that care where the work is done. The falsifier is a Valtech statement of onshore delivery, or a client case crediting a named onshore team, at the next compile.

Second, AI visibility: Valtech sells a GEO QuickStart on Adobe's tool but has no audited AI visibility product of its own in the record; a rival with a citation share scorecard can, likely, take that purchase from the shared clients (Mars, Decathlon, Mandarin Oriental, Volvo Trucks, ABB Robotics, Mitchells & Butlers) that already buy marketing elsewhere. Third, the evidence gap is the widest in the top ten: 19 of 20 clients carry no described work, so a rival pitching Audi, Dolby or Dunelm can ask what the platform delivered. Fourth, the machine-readable layer: no feed, schema or entity work in the record on a core web and commerce line, roughly even chance that a structured data and entity offer around its commerce builds is taken up. Fifth, no public pricing model, so an outcome priced offer is a conversation Valtech cannot have in public.
